subject: Subscripts
notes: The subscript general format has exactly THREE alternatives and each now has a witness. ALL - pb62 (the three ranges GR1a defers to; vacuous at 85, which has no function for which the subscript ALL is allowed). index-name-1 [{+|-} integer-1] - 85/index_name_r7_windows and pb170. arithmetic-expression-1 - pb136 for compound expressions and pb877_subscripted_subscript for the shape that had no vehicle until kb/Work PB877: an identifier operand carrying its OWN subscripts. 8.8.1.1 admits 'an identifier referencing a numeric data item' and 8.4.3.1.2 Format 2 makes that identifier a qualified-data-name-WITH-SUBSCRIPTS, so X(1) is an arithmetic-expression-1 - but the declaration-informed '(' splitter asked DataItem.IsTable, which is only the first half of 8.4.2.3.3 SR2, so the identifier's own '(' opened a SECOND subscript and every such reference failed arity. It was loud on the receiving side (COBOL0899) and a run-time abort on the sending side. Format 1 (qualified-data-name-with-subscripts) and Format 2 (qualified-condition-name-with-subscripts) are both covered: the golden subscripts data-names, and ResolveForItem - the condition-name path, whose subscripts identify the occurrence of the CONDITIONAL VARIABLE - applies the same SR2/SR3 screen. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/ReferenceResolver.cs#SplitSubscriptTokens (kb/Work PB2113: the subscript list is the grammar's subscriptList, read by SegmentsOf) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/ReferenceResolver.cs#MaterializeViaFragment (replaced: kb/Work PB2151 reads the position's parse node into a typed Position (BindPosition, MaterializePosition); RenderSegment and the text re-parse are deleted) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/ReferenceResolver.cs#RenderSegment (replaced: kb/Work PB2151 reads the position's parse node into a typed Position (BindPosition, MaterializePosition); RenderSegment and the text re-parse are deleted)
